non_claims: a passing regeneration records that the measurement planes were re-run from the frozen candidate and the frozen toolchain, that each now binds the current venue manifest and that each reproduced its evidence on a second run; it is a reproducibility statement, never a memory-safety claim, and it is never read as 'the candidate is memory safe'

the determinism claim is on each plane's *evidence* (its `body`, with the per-run fields the plane declares normalised), not on its whole envelope: a plane's envelope legitimately differs in the pathless non-committed inputs a tool records, so `bytes_identical` is recorded as a fact and never read as the claim

it re-runs the planes' own `--measure` and never edits a plane by hand, so it can neither widen nor narrow what a plane reports; the planes' own findings survive the regeneration unchanged, and a `PASS` that did not survive is recorded as a finding rather than suppressed

a plane whose instrument the venue cannot run is recorded un-re-measured with its exact reason and an open residual, never silently accepted and never counted clean; the `MS-CLEAN-REGEN` court refuses such a plane that is not so recorded

reproducibility is not reproducibility across venues: it shows the committed evidence is what the toolchain on the admitted base derives, not that a different toolchain or machine would derive the same evidence

the regeneration re-runs the measurement planes; it does not re-run the pure derivation planes (25.3-25.8, 25.13-25.15, 25.17-25.18), which `evidence_determinism.py` already re-derives from committed inputs without a compiler

rule.determinism_rule: a plane is reproducible when the second `--measure` derives the same evidence as the committed plane -- its `body`, with the declared per-run fields normalised; the claim is admitted only when both evidence digests exist and agree
rule.evidence_rule: the determinism claim is on the plane's evidence, not its whole envelope: the pathless non-committed inputs a tool records (a raw compiler stream), the per-run transcript digest Miri records and the build-product test-binary fields ASan/TSan record are not evidence, and the plane names each one
rule.manifest_rule: every plane must record the current `forensics/memory-safety/container.json` digest as an input; a plane still binding a superseded digest is a residual, never a pass
rule.procedure_rule: each plane is regenerated by its own `--measure`, in dependency order (the census first, then the planes that consume it), and never edited by hand: the regeneration can neither widen nor narrow what a plane reports
rule.sort_key: planes in procedure order; residuals by residual_id
rule.subject: the measurement planes the memory-safety stratum ships: the source census, the non-Rust TCB, Miri, ASan/MSan, TSan, Kani and the CVE-replay index
rule.survival_rule: a plane's evidence is compared with the evidence committed at HEAD; a plane that did not survive is a finding, so a PASS that did not survive the regeneration is named rather than silently replaced
rule.venue_rule: each plane runs in exactly the venue its own subphase admitted: the court's default per-process RLIMIT_DATA, except ASan and TSan, which take the manifest's documented `OPENSSL_RS_COURT_DATA=unlimited` override
